tagline: the real cost of a car
storage_hint: Disk used by the installation (Raspberry Pi limit)
fuel_stale: The fuel price is more than 30 days old
load_failed: The data could not be loaded.
footer: Unknown values are shown as pending, never as 0. Notes and the log are kept in English; listing captures stay in their original language.
open_dossier_aria: Open the dossier and photos of {u}
delta_help: Only computed when both this car and your car have a complete TCO; comparing partial subtotals would mislead.
price_change_title: Change of the asking price since the first capture ({d})
units_lead: Every car for sale against the one you own: costs over the period you chose, {n} cost components, and the score from your ranking weights.
ranking_hint: The score comes from the questionnaire and the weights on the Ranking page.
no_units: No cars yet. Cars are added by capturing a listing (an agent does this from a link you send).
pin_ref: Pin my car at the top
hide_over_budget: Hide cars over the maximum budget
composition_lead: {y} · {km} km. Hover a segment to see the amount.
cost_pick_lead: Choose which costs count; cars missing any selected cost are marked incomplete and go last.
chart_note: Common scale for every car. Pending amounts have no size because they are unknown; the Details view is the data view.
dep_help: Candidate: asking price − resale at the end. Your car: sale today − resale at the end (the opportunity cost of keeping it).
be_title: Break-even: keep your car or switch
be_lead: Month-by-month cash view. Buying starts with the upfront outlay (price + purchase costs − what your car fetches today) and adds the car's running costs; keeping adds your car's. Where the lines cross, the switch has paid for itself. At the end each line drops by its resale value.
be_missing_title: Data is still missing for these cars:
be_note: Running costs (fuel, insurance, tax, maintenance, repairs, tyres) are spread evenly over the months; repairs and tyres are not dated yet. The vertical drop in the last month is the resale value (and, for your car, its selling costs).
be_hi_lead: Cars in the chart (click a car to show or hide it; the table lists all):
be_hi_hint: Show or hide this car in the chart
preview_banner: Preview: the parameters have been changed in Settings but not saved.
ranking_lead: Cars for sale ranked by what matters to you. Each bar shows how much each criterion contributed. Fuel, insurance and tax live inside the total cost, so nothing counts twice; missing data lowers the coverage and never counts as 0. Your own car is scored the same way and shown for comparison, without a rank.
need_two: The ranking needs at least two cars for sale with data in the weighted criteria.
quiz_lead: Eight quick choices between four cars. Each time the cars are the same model and equal in everything except one advantage each. Tap the one you would buy, then the one you would buy last. There are no right answers; Carlos counts what you pick and shows you the count afterwards.
weights_lead: Move a slider to override the answers. The ranking then shows the weights were set by hand, and you can go back to the answers at any time.
ranking_edit: Change the questionnaire or the weights
formula_text: For each criterion with weight > 0 and at least two cars with a value: score = (value − worst) ÷ (best − worst), so the best car gets 100. Car score = Σ weight × score ÷ Σ weights of the criteria this car has a value for. Coverage = the share of the total weight that could be scored.
why_fewer_than_two_cars_with_a_value: fewer than two cars with a value
cb_cost_month: Total cost ÷ months, including the loss of value (depreciation): fuel, insurance, tax, maintenance, repairs, tyres, purchase/sale costs and depreciation. Unknown while one is missing.
cb_cash_now: Asking price plus the purchase costs of this car.
cb_reliability: Known weak points in four parts: engine (incl. intake, cooling, turbo, injection), gearbox & clutch, chassis & brakes, electrics. Each part starts at 9 points and loses the severity points of its 3 worst weak points (HIGH 3, MEDIUM 2, HIGH IF APPLICABLE 1.5, LOW-MEDIUM 1, LOW 0.5), so more documentation never makes a car look worse. A recall costs its points until its check at the viewing says it was done. Score out of 36; higher is better.
rel_no_part: Not assigned to a part yet (reliability unknown)
rel_lead: Each part starts at 9 and loses the points of its 3 worst weak points (HIGH 3, MEDIUM 2, recall 1.5, LOW-MEDIUM 1, LOW 0.5); the reliability score is the sum, out of 36. A recall costs its points until the checklist shows it was done.
cb_inspection: Checklist items marked as a problem at a viewing; unknown until something was checked.
cb_confidence: Share of the research contract done for this car (its generation, engine, variant and listing): verified items count 1, estimated or C/D-source items ½, missing items 0.
gaps_note: The agent's to-do list (always in English).
mp_lead: Scheduled jobs for your period ({km} km, {m} months). Each job counts period ÷ interval (an expected value: a used car's position in its cycle is unknown); a job done at purchase restarts its schedule.
mp_none: No item schedule for this model yet.
rs_due_x: Not documented as done and due now, so the job is paid at purchase (counted once as a certain maintenance cost).
rs_claim_x: The seller claims this job was done; it is not verified yet (ask for the invoice, see the checklist). Without proof, its cost is added after the viewing.
rs_documented_x: The service record shows this job was done recently.
rs_effect: The schedule starts again from this job: only full intervals after it count in your period.
rk_lead: Each risk fails with a probability somewhere in a km window; the car is exposed to the share of the window it drives through in your period.
viewing_hint: Tick the checklist, write notes and take photos while looking at the car. Everything is saved at once.
log_ph: Note for the log (in English, please)
no_reliability: No reliability data for this model.
no_archive: No captures yet. Once the listing is archived, its description, features and photos stay here even after it disappears.
dossier_failed: The dossier could not be loaded: {m}
window_hint: Applies only to cars first registered in this window (e.g. before or after the facelift, a recall's build range)
level_hint: The level this row is attached to: the variant, its engine or its generation
research_lead: What must be known on each level (the research contract) and how much of it is done. A level counts as researched when nothing is missing.
levels_hint: a row attached to an engine or a generation applies to every variant that shares it
models_lead: Make → model → generation → engine → variant. Maintenance, risks and watch points are attached to the right level and inherited by every variant below.
title: Title
sources_lead: Every data point is linked to a source with a quality A–D (A official, B ADAC/TÜV/manuals, C aggregators, D forums and snippets).
settings_lead: The assumptions behind every cost in the comparison, the look of the app and your account.
calc_group_hint: Changes preview immediately in the comparison; nothing is saved until you press Save.
profile_hint: The profile used for insurance quotes (by the agent). It does not enter the cost calculation.
h_acquisition: Leasing counts the lease payments, fees and extra km instead of the price and resale. A lease rate rarely includes insurance: lessors require fully comprehensive cover (Vollkasko).
h_lease_rate_max: Leave empty if you only buy.
lease_note: A lease is costed over its term: payments instead of price and resale, fees and extra km instead of purchase costs. Damage found at the return is not predicted. Without insurance in the rate, a Vollkasko quote is needed.
appearance_hint: Every theme shows the same data in the same places; only the look changes. Remembered in this browser.
theme_friendly_hint: Clean, soft blue, rounded, easy on the eyes
theme_kawaii_hint: Pastel pink and mint, round corners, dots
theme_circuit_hint: PCB green, copper traces, LED statuses; dark only
theme_arcade_hint: Black maze, blue walls, pellet dots, Pac-Man yellow; dark only
theme_garage_hint: Asphalt black, signal yellow, tyre-tread texture; dark only
theme_terminal_hint: Phosphor green and amber on black, monospace
theme_olive_hint: Olive, brass and cream, workshop-manual feel
agent_token_hint: The token an agent uses to write data into this account (Authorization: Bearer). It is shown once; creating a new one disables the old one. Creating a new token also invalidates the one in .env; give the new one to your agent.
token_shown_once: Copy it now; it will not be shown again.
admin_lead: Accounts, research workers, the research queue and every change. Admins see every account's data, including notes and viewing data.
create_invite: Create and get the invite link
invite_created: Invite link for {u} (valid 72 hours, one use):
versus_none: No car for sale has a complete cost yet.
versus_hint: Ranked first by your weights, complete cost of ownership.
ruler_title: Cost per month, every car on one scale
ruler_lead: Your car is the dashed line. Cars left of it cost less per month, cars right of it more. A filled marker is a complete cost of ownership; a hollow one is a partial subtotal and sits where its known costs put it.
plate_score_note: Calculated from your answers to the preferences form (Ranking page).
plate_rel_note: Each part starts at 9 and loses the points of its 3 worst known weak points. Higher is better.
quiz_method: How the choices become weights: each advantage appears in exactly four of the eight choices, and every two advantages meet at least once. For each one, Carlos counts how often you picked its car first and how often last: (first − last) ÷ times shown gives −1 to +1, which maps to 0–5, never below 1 (only you can switch a criterion off, by hand). An advantage you never saw counts 3. This is best–worst scaling, a standard survey method that forces trade-offs instead of asking how important things are, because everything is "important" when asked directly. Details and sources: docs/ranking.md.
prio_lead: How much each criterion counts in the score, 0 to 5, and the answers behind it.
prio_none_text: Every criterion counts the same until you make eight quick choices between cars (about three minutes).
prio_manual_text: These weights were set by hand, so they no longer follow your answers.
prio_skipped: You skipped the choices; every criterion counts the same for now. Make them on the Ranking page whenever you like.
sl_drive: The distance and the years you keep the car set the period every cost is calculated over.
sl_money: The budget marks cars as over budget; the fuel prices feed the running costs.
st_search: Where and what are you looking for?
sl_search: Agents use this when they look for listings for you. It does not change any calculation.
sl_insurance: Cover, history and discounts: the rest of what a quote needs.
sl_workshop: Jobs you do yourself are costed as parts only, with the hours shown separately. Everything else is priced at a workshop.
sl_priorities: Eight quick choices between four cars, about three minutes. Each time, tap the car you would buy and then the one you would buy last.
done_lead: This is what Carlos will work with. Everything can be changed later in Settings or by running this setup again.
setup_again_text: The setup walks through everything Carlos needs from you: driving, money, search, insurance profile, workshop and priorities.
h_annual_km: Not sure? Take two service invoices or inspection reports: the kilometre difference divided by the years between them.
h_ownership_years: Depreciation, wear and the break-even are calculated over this period.
h_driving_mix: Helps check the consumption figures of each car against how you drive.
h_current_car: Carlos compares every car for sale against it.
h_budget_ideal: What you would like to spend.
h_budget_max: The most you would spend for the right car.
h_fuel: Today's prices at your usual station. Saving updates the price date.
ins_privacy: Stored only in your account and used only when you ask for insurance quotes. No names or addresses.
h_age: If several people drive the car, the youngest one sets the price.
h_sf: On your current policy. Roughly one class per claim-free year; new drivers start at SF 0 or SF 1/2.
h_cover: Liability covers damage to others. Partial cover adds theft, glass, storm and animals. Comprehensive also covers damage you cause to your own car.
p_premium_now: What you pay now per year (€, optional)
h_premium_now: Your current car's premium, used as its insurance cost.
p_claims: Claims in the last three years
h_diy: Untick everything if a workshop does all the work.
sl_drivers: Insurers price the policyholder and every regular driver. These are the questions the comparison sites ask.
h_drivers: Only people who drive the car regularly.
h_licence_date: Category B, the date on the licence.
h_occupation: Some groups (public service, civil servants) get cheaper tariffs.
p_other_car: Has another car of their own
h_other_car: Insured separately, in their own name.
h_ins_start: Usually the day you register the car.
h_workshop_binding: Cheaper if the insurer picks the workshop for repairs.
h_prev_insurer: Leave empty if this is your first car.
bw_frame: Four cars of the same model, equal in everything except the highlighted line.
bw_ask_worst: And which one would you buy last?
bw_ask_done: Your order. Tap a car to change it.
bw_equal: Anything not shown is the same for all four.
bw_month_note: €40 a month is {v} over your {y} years.
bw_row_cost_month: Total cost per month (incl. loss of value)
bw_row_reliability: Known weak points of this model
bw_rel_base: One known weak point (its repair is already in the total cost)
bw_insp_base: Two small faults (price lowered to cover them)
tally_none: You skipped every choice that showed this.
prio_retired_text: Your earlier answers were for a previous version of the questions, so every criterion counts the same until you make the eight new choices (about three minutes).
ruler_waiting: No cost is known yet for any car. Costs fill in as each car is researched (consumption, maintenance, risks, tyres, tax, insurance); open a car to see what is still missing.
provisional_note: Scores marked ? are provisional: less than half of what you weight is known for that car yet. They firm up as the research fills in.
provisional_hint: Provisional: less than half of the weighted data is known.
h_keeper: The person in whose name the car is registered.
from_drivers_step: Set from the people in the setup's Drivers step
req_lead: Paste the link of a listing. The shared research worker reads it, researches the car and adds it to your cars; follow it here.
req_queue_lead: Every request of every account: who asked, when, and what came of it.
st_charging: If you went electric: where would you charge?
sl_charging: Only electric cars use this, for the cost of their energy. Leave it empty if electric cars are not an option.
hc_wallbox_planned: Not yet, I would install a wallbox
h_home_pct: The rest is charged at public chargers. A normal socket loses about 10 % more energy than a wallbox (ADAC).
h_wallbox_cost: Only if you would install one: usually €1,000–3,500; no federal KfW grant in 2026, ask your Stadtwerke.
h_elec_home: From your bill; the German average is about 0.37 €/kWh (BDEW 2026).
h_elec_public: What you pay at public chargers: with a contract about 0.47–0.55 €/kWh (AC); ad hoc often 0.52 AC / 0.70 DC (ADAC 2026).
viewing_as: Viewing as {u}: you see this account exactly as its owner does; changes are logged with your name.
workers_lead: Each worker polls the queue with its own token; down = no heartbeat for 3 minutes.
worker_token_hint: Token for {n}, shown once: give it to the worker as WORKER_TOKEN.
changes_lead: Every write through the API: who, for which account, what and when.
